newsitem.title: USA: Koll bondholders offer to take equity.
newsitem.headline: Koll bondholders offer to take equity.

text.p: Koll Real Estate Group bondholders said on Thursday that they are offering to exchange the $183 million principal amount of outstanding 12 percent debentures for 90 percent of the company's common stock.
The remaining 10 percent would be divided between the common and preferred shareholders in a manner agreeable to them, Koll bondholders said in a statement.
Koll Real Estate company representatives were not immediately available for comment.

Wilbur Ross Jr, senior managing director of Rothschild, said in a statement that Koll is over leveraged and that is reflecting upon the stock price and its debentures being valued at 55 percent of par.
Ross said the proposal will provide KREG with a proper capital structure.
The restructured company would then borrow $25,000,000 to develop and construct Bolsa Chica in Huntington Beach, Calif., the bondholders, who are being advised by Rothschild Inc, said.
In addition, management would be granted options to purchase 5 percent of the reorganized company's stock, the company said.
The bondholders also requested that their majority ownership of the stock entitle them to majority representation on the board, they said.
